mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS against 20-day forward returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 300, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the average 20-day return in these periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A tight labor market (UNRATE below 3.5%) combined with weak consumer spending (RSAFS below 660,000) indicates an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (UNRATE * RSAFS) does not produce a significant negative Rank IC (below 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window, or the negative returns predicted by the interaction occur in less than 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined as FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.0% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: In the 3-month periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, the S&P 500 has positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the average return in these periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A stronger labor market (measured by PAYEMS) indicates robust economic activity and higher consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS against 60-day forward returns falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 100 (the 2017 base index), it signals a strengthening supply chain and economic expansion, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO exceeds 100, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the average 5-day return in these periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) does not produce a significant positive Rank IC (above 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window, or the positive returns predicted by the interaction occur in less than 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market and reduced consumer confidence, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST is below 1400, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the average 60-day return in these periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
